## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Buddhasabbaññubhāvapañha* ("Omniscience and Why The Buddha Changed His Mind", Mil 5.4.10) is an inquiry in the *Milindapañha* concerning the nature of the Buddha's omniscience [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records three modern translations of the text in three languages [SuttaCentral]. It also associates the text with several related canonical and paracanonical discourses and treatises, noting mentions or thematic connections with the *Cātuma Sutta* (MN 67), the *Sammāsambuddhasutta* (SN 22.58), multiple sections of the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 8, Mnd 14, Mnd 16), the *Cullaniddesa* (Cnd 19), the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 3.1 *Mahāpaññākathā*), the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37 *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*), and another section of the *Milindapañha* itself, the *Magguppādanapañha* (Mil 5.5.4) [SuttaCentral].
Computational analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 46 internal text-reuse matches between the *Buddhasabbaññubhāvapañha* and eight other sections of the *Milindapañha*, largely consisting of recurring dialogue formulations [DharmaNexus]. Its closest internal alignment partners include the *Sabbasattahitapharaṇapañha* (Mil 5.3.2; 10 matches), the *Buddhalābhantarāyapañha* (Mil 5.2.5; 7 matches), the *Pharusavācābhāvapañha* (Mil 5.3.4; 6 matches), and the *Dhammadesanāyaappossukkapañha* (Mil 5.5.10; 6 matches), with additional shared phrasing found in Mil 5.3.12, Mil 5.3.7, Mil 5.2.7, and Mil 5.1.9 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus reports no cross-language matches with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [DharmaNexus].
